gaps: P0: only a generic Nuremberg Chronicle stock woodcut (Rijksmuseum says it is a city view ‘here used as’ Pisa); P1: only a town plan across a book gutter (#3) and Vasari’s ceiling, whose view is of Siena (#4); P2: only a map (#5)
notes: #17: the mount says the original was received from the Military Intelligence Division and returned in July 1920, so the photo dates from the 1910s (World War I era); drop it if that is too loose. #20 is a 2025 photo of the same Hackert painting as #9. #7 (1834) and #8 (1801) show the Piazza dei Cavalieri. #13/#14 (1913, from the tower) are faded red-toned prints. #19 (2012) is shot through a streaked window.
